It explicitly refuses to bind those later results to the exact C4 source line because the target file has no later recoverable version/hash and the R2 main record has no HitTestMode literal.

omissions.finding: The report acknowledges later build/install only through main-session and child-agent claims; it does not open or cite the stronger native builder output at R2 physical line 7694 (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 12 s 22 ms` and `HAP installed`). This is recoverable because the report already reaches the correct non-binding boundary.

The report could distinguish more sharply between main-session statements, child-agent summaries, file/path existence, and direct device command output. It generally labels these as claims, so this is annotation precision rather than overclaimed closure.

yaml_semantics.finding: `entry: []` is justified because changed blame cannot identify who introduced Block. The fixing main@v252 is correctly `正常`, and unbound later R2 evidence is correctly `无法确认`. The separately declared R1 v253 node is invalid, as detailed below.

`agent:__main__:01a009fe@v253` is out of range: the ledger has main versions 1..252. Search rendered tail activity as `喂 v253 (锚点之后)`, but that synthetic tail/feed label is not a valid agent node coordinate. The R1 post-patch validation actions may be cited as later boundary evidence, but must not be materialized as agent@v253.
yaml_semantics.audit: _migloop-eval-20260909/attribution10/audits-v3/codex-c4.json reports nodes 3/4 resolved and diagnoses v253 as 版本越界(1..252).

yaml_semantics.finding: The v253 node cites `#...:4618@L8096`, but action #4618 is physically at lines 8100-8101; physical line 8096 is a different response item. The audit therefore records one missing evidence reference.

The node `agent:__main__:01a021e5@v181` cites physical line 6505/action #7439, which belongs to main v185. That later action is legitimate post-v181 boundary evidence, but it was not input available to agent@v181. The reason should label it explicitly as subsequent evidence or use a v185 boundary node; the current grouping is ambiguous rather than proof that the semantic conclusion is wrong.

Listing repaired file@v2 as a `正常` node is allowed by the current interpretation: the prohibition is against marking repair.after as a red/faulty node. The GUIDE wording can read ambiguously, so this may be redundant, but it is not graded as an error.
The parsed verdict has zero schema errors and complete empty coverage, but those checks do not authenticate the behavioural or temporal claims above.

improvements: V2 had zero full-pool searches; V3 performs four post-patch full-pool searches with explicit since/until timestamps.
V3 opens index(kind=time), identifies both allowed session groups, and then searches the R2 main agent through v231.
V3 does not use pipe-separated pseudo-OR terms; tool output also explicitly states that search is literal.
remaining_issues: The full-pool term `hvigor` is broad and reports only the earliest match per agent, which is an R2 system-prompt hit rather than the later build result.
The subsequent R2 term `install` returns 26,022 characters and many unrelated hits. The run opens earlier install statements instead of the direct #7859/L7694 builder result.
Most search text remains actor-scoped: 12/16 searches and 115,361/119,995 search characters. This is not wrong after R2 discovery, but it is inefficient.

time_scope_review.finding: The chosen upper bound, 2026-08-22T15:24:42.229Z, is later than the known R2 line-7694 build/install, and later agent@v231 searches have no time cutoff; therefore the omission of that anchor was not caused by the upper bound excluding it.
time_scope_review.correction: The full-pool zero-hit query used the literal `点击同意`; the later 20-hit R2-agent query used the different literal `同意并继续`. These results are not comparable evidence of a cutoff defect. The run makes no `agent(until=<action sequence>)` call—the mechanism recently fixed—so this adjudication cannot attribute anything to that bug.
time_scope_review.remaining_boundary: Time index warns that some action times may be missing or unsortable, so time-bounded searches retain their stated scope limits; no specific C4 failure from that condition was reproduced here.
